title: TSM Plans $500M Investment in Anthropic IPO: Will the Pivot Pay Off? - TradingView
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited TSM is strengthening its exposure to the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence (AI) market through investments in other technology behemoths, thereby maintaining visibility into the emerging computing requirements. In addition to augmenting its position in the AI ecosystem, the investments are likely to create opportunities for financial returns, deepen industry relationships and support long-term semiconductor demand. TSM has proposed a $500 million investment in Anthropic's initial public offering (IPO). The investment comes as Anthropic targets an IPO price range of $70-$78 per share, potentially valuing the AI startup at approximately $1.4 trillion. TSM also approved an investment of up to $500 million in OpenAI's preferred shares, bringing its combined potential investment in the two AI developers to $1 billion. Anthropic IPO 2026 Guide: Price Predictions, Dates, and Everything You Need to Know As the world's largest contract chipmaker and a key supplier of advanced processors used in AI infrastructure, TSM is well-positioned to benefit from the growing computational requirements of generative AI applications. The move complements TSM's ongoing investments in advanced manufacturing technologies and packaging capabilities to address rising demand for high-performance computing chips. However, the proposed investment also introduces exposure to the valuation and execution risks associated with rapidly growing AI developers. Anthropic's substantial valuation and elevated infrastructure spending requirements raise questions about the sustainability of returns as competition intensifies across the AI industry. Moreover, TSM continues to face significant capital expenditure requirements to expand its advanced manufacturing capacity, making disciplined capital allocation increasingly important. Nevertheless, the proposed investment represents an opportunity for TSM to participate more directly in the long-term growth of the AI ecosystem, potentially complementing its established leadership in semiconductor manufacturing and supporting its growth prospects.
